item.description:
- **Updates reach the newest version sooner.** Changmun now looks for updates every hour instead of once a day, and each time it opens. A version already downloaded and waiting is still installed when you quit, so if a newer one came out after it, that one follows the next time you open and quit. - **Fixed:** in a tab a page opened with `about:blank;`, Back no longer leads to a white page. On the first real page of such a tab, Back is off, as in other browsers.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy. Hourly and at-launch checks only start from this version, so they haven't run against a real newer release yet, and swiping back in such a tab hasn't been tried by hand.

- **Keep translating a site.** Turn on "Keep translating this site" in the site settings over the address, or by right-clicking the translate button, and its foreign pages translate by themselves as you go from one to the next. Text a page adds later, as you scroll, is translated too. Show Original counts for that page only. It works on the exact address you turned it on for, with or without www, and never in a private window. Pages in your own language are left alone. - **With Claude, this sends each page's text to Anthropic without a click,** so it has limits. A page and what it adds later share one allowance, a site can send at most 300,000 characters in ten minutes on its own, and a page that keeps reloading itself is stopped there. Pages with a password, one-time code or card field are never sent, and a tab you aren't looking at sends no added text. - **Translating no longer writes over text a site has changed in the meantime,** and Show Original leaves such text as it is.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy. The new switch and menu on screen, keeping going with translation on this Mac, and pages restored with Back haven't been tried by hand, so tell me what looks or feels off.

- **Translate pages with Claude.** If Claude Code is set up on your Mac, you can pick Claude and a model for page translation in Settings › General, next to translation on this Mac. It is off by default. The page's text goes to Anthropic, and the translate button says so while it works. Private windows and other profiles' pages stay on this Mac. Pages with a password, one-time code or card field are never sent, and neither is text you can't see. Claude runs with no tools, and a translation that brings an address, a link or a long number the page didn't have is thrown away. If only part of a page was translated, the status line says so. - **Favorites show which ones are open by their color.** A favorite with no tab is faded, so the open ones stand out, in the sidebar and in tabs on top. The dot under the tile is gone.
Tried with automated tests, and with one call to the real claude outside the app. A real translation through the app, the new tooltip and messages on screen, and macOS 14 and 15 haven't been tried by hand, so tell me what looks or feels off.

- **A design pass over the whole app.** Six text sizes instead of twenty-three, four corner radii, three shadows, and one kind of main button. All spacing now sits on an 8-point grid, so sidebar rows are 32 points tall and a screen shows slightly fewer tabs. Faint text is darker and easier to read. Switching tabs from the keyboard no longer animates, and a selected tab's title no longer changes weight. Checks now keep these rules from drifting. - **Dialogs are clearer and safer.** Questions about deleting, opening another app, the camera, signing in and extensions share one design: a short question, one sentence, verbs on the buttons. The filled button is always the one Return presses, and it is the safe choice. When a page, an extension or the AI asks, Allow stays locked for half a second, so a timed click can't land on it. A page you block can't ask again until it reloads, dialogs no longer stack, and long addresses are cut from the left so the real domain stays visible. An extension's prompt never grants more than it shows. A web page's own alert, confirm and prompt stay system dialogs. - **The AI's approval card has a clear order:** Don't Allow is the strong button, Allow Once sits beside it, and allowing for the chat is a quiet link. - **A friendlier first run.** One question to start, what will be brought over stated in one line, and it always ends ready to use: without Claude Code the browser works right away and the AI can wait. - **The certificate warning leads with what matters.** The title, the site and the reason come first, and the details and Visit This Website are under Show Details. Warnings that a certificate changed stay in view. - **A new app icon:** a larger window, with its arched light and the shadow of its bars falling on the floor. - **A new homepage,** in ink on white, that shows the product on the first screen. On a phone it offers to send the link to your Mac. - **Clearer Korean,** in one voice throughout. - **Fixed:** with many favorites, the start page's row no longer runs past the page.
Tried with automated tests and the headless copy. The dialogs' real look on screen, pressed buttons, Korean IME, VoiceOver and the homepage on a real iPhone haven't been tried by hand, so tell me what looks or feels off.

- **The AI reads pages better.** Two new tools sit next to `read_page`. `read_structured` gives the facts a page carries about itself (JSON-LD, OpenGraph and Twitter tags, description, language, canonical and alternate links) as compact JSON, with no page text and no request to the network, so a price, an author or a date costs almost nothing to find out. `read_markdown` gives the visible content as Markdown, keeping tables, nested lists, code blocks with their language, and links (paths on the same site, tracking parameters out). It isn't always shorter than `read_page`; it keeps the structure. `read_page` is still what numbers things to click. All three work from the AI panel, MCP and the `changmun` CLI (`changmun structured`, `changmun markdown`), under the same approvals. - **A site's own Markdown version.** When a page points to a Markdown version of itself on its own site (a `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` address in the same language), `read_markdown` reads that instead and says so, with a note that it may differ from what you see on screen. - **Secrets stay out of what the AI reads.** In both tools, parameters named like tokens, keys, signatures, sessions and passwords have their values hidden in addresses, sign-in fragments are dropped, and invisible characters are stripped. - **Dropping at the end of a group or folder is tidier.** The place to drop only appears while you drag, so groups have no extra gap at rest, and it is now in the tab strip too. Links dragged in from a page go on the group's header, which puts them at its end. (The drag itself still has not been tried by hand, so tell me if it doesn't take.) - **Unpinning a folder** keeps the tabs of an inner folder that is still pinned where they are. - **Start page:** the unread dot sits beside the title instead of floating in the middle of the page. - **README:** a comparison with Safari, Chrome, Arc and Dia, with what Changmun doesn't do yet, and the app's real size (21 MB, about 7 MB to download).

- **Fixed: ↑/↓ in the start page's search field.** With something typed, the arrow keys (and ⇥) moved the focus among the sections behind the suggestion list instead of choosing a suggestion; they now choose one, and with nothing typed ↓ still goes down into the sections. - **Fixed: unpinning a folder from the sidebar no longer makes its open tabs vanish.** The tabs of a folder's bookmarks show only where the folder is, so unpinning it hid them everywhere. They now come back to the tab list as a group named for the folder (a lone one as a plain tab); the folder stays among your bookmarks. - **A place to drop at the end of a group or a folder.** Items could only be dropped just above a row, so a tab could never be put last in a group, nor a bookmark last in a folder. A thin strip below the last row of an open group or folder now takes the drop and puts it at the end. (Tried through the code only; the drag itself is not yet tried by hand, so tell me if it does not take. The tab strip on top still has no such place.)

- **Bookmarks inside a folder can be put in order.** Drag a bookmark in a sidebar folder and drop it on another row of the same folder to place it just above that row; drop it on the folder itself to send it to the end. A bookmark dragged in from another folder lands at the row you drop it on. Folders you have never arranged stay exactly as they were imported, and a bookmark added or moved in later goes last. (Tabs and links dropped on a row of a folder now go into that folder, as if dropped on the folder. Tried through the code and the saved order; the drag itself is not yet tried by hand, so tell me if it doesn't take.)

- **A start page of your own.** A new tab, a new window and an empty space now open a start page instead of a blank bar: a search field that takes addresses, searches and questions for the AI, your favorites as tiles, "Continue viewing" (recently closed tabs and recent pages), your Reading List, frequently visited sites, and a row of things to ask the AI. ⌘T opens a tab showing it with the search field ready; ⌘L still goes to the address. - **Make it yours.** Three styles (Dashboard, Quiet, AI First); turn each section on or off, drag them into the order you like, and set per-section options. Pick the background: the space's colour glow, plain, one of eight colours or your own, or one picture of yours (shrunk and stripped of its metadata, with a veil that keeps the text readable). Choose what a new tab opens: the start page, the command bar, a blank page or an address you set. Customize from the page itself, from View › Customize Start Page…, or in Settings › Start Page. - **Private by design.** A private window's start page shows no history, closed tabs, Reading List or AI suggestions, and ignores a custom new-tab address. The AI, MCP, the command-line tool and extensions see a start tab as a blank page and never read what it shows. Items you hide from the page are kept only as salted hashes, and are wiped when you clear history or site data. - **Clearing history now also forgets recently closed tabs**, so they no longer come back on the start page. - **Fixed:** a private window's search suggestions no longer list pages from your normal history. (The picture, the layout and the options are tried headlessly; the blur, the Customize popover's look, drag-to-reorder and typing with a Korean keyboard are not yet tried by hand, so tell me what looks or feels off.)

- **Works with VoiceOver and the keyboard.** The sidebar, tab strip, page bar, command bar, find bar, AI panel, approval cards, settings and the untrusted-certificate warning now have names, states and actions; rows that were only clickable can be pressed from the keyboard and by VoiceOver; status messages (undo, downloads, translation, load errors) are announced. An audit that dumps the app's own accessibility tree found 113 unnamed controls before and none after, and the look is unchanged. (Not yet tried with a real VoiceOver session, so tell me what reads oddly.) - **Reading List.** Save a page for later from Bookmarks › Add to Reading List (⇧⌘D), a tab's menu or a link's menu; the list sits at the top of the bookmarks popover with unread pages in bold, marks pages read when you open them, and comes along when you import from Safari. It is never shown to the AI and never kept from private windows. - **Tracking removed from addresses you open.** Known tracking parameters (utm_*, fbclid, gclid and the like) are taken out of addresses you type, bookmarks, links you open in a new tab or peek, and what the AI opens. Links you click inside a page are left alone, because rewriting them from outside the engine would weaken sites' cross-site cookie protection. Switch in Settings › Privacy, and per site in the site's settings. - **Prefer secure connections.** An http:// address you open is tried over https first and falls back to http only if the site refuses or drops the connection, never after a certificate error. Switch in Settings › Privacy. - **Clearing site data now really clears your saved sign-ins.** A sign-in snapshot taken a moment before you cleared site data (or removed a profile, or turned "Stay signed in after quitting" off) could still be written afterwards and come back at the next launch. That race, in 0.8.7, is closed, and a test now hammers it.

- **Sign-ins survive quitting.** Many sites keep you signed in with a cookie meant to end when the browser closes, so closing Changmun signed you out of them every time. Those session cookies are now kept, encrypted with a key in your login Keychain, for up to 30 days and put back before your windows open. Settings › Privacy › "Stay signed in after quitting" turns it off (which also deletes them); clearing site data deletes them too, private windows never keep any, and the Agent copy doesn't keep sign-ins. - **Stay open after the last window closes, if you like.** Settings › General › "Quit when the last window is closed" is on, as before; turn it off and Changmun keeps running like Safari, and the Dock icon or ⌘N brings back your last session.
